lines.text: Relax, new guy, I brought you a coffee. Not from Café Lantern, sadly. So — Seiran Academy, huh? Told you to ask about ten years ago.

...Hinako Mori. *Her jokes vanish; she stares at the letter.* I knew her. She came to the Seiran newspaper club — I was a first-year, fifteen. She brought a notebook about the reflection room, begged us to print it, and I told her it wasn't my decision. We never printed anything. A week later she fell off the annex roof, and the school called it an accident.

That's her. That's Hinako in the photo — I'd know her face anywhere. Ishida was her homeroom teacher, writing 'forgive me'... Detective, whoever circled that face knew exactly what she was carrying, and I don't think it was guilt that kept him quiet for ten years.

'Someone from the old days.' So Ishida knew it was coming and still opened the door. Ten years of cowards, Detective — everyone from that school kept their mouths shut until people started dying. Question is who finally scared them enough to talk.

Mori. Hinako was on duty that day... *She pulls a plastic sleeve from her bag, hands trembling slightly.* Take it. Two months ago, before the first body, this turned up in my mailbox — no stamp, no name. Unfolded, it said: 'Ask them about Hinako Mori.' I thought it was a tip, a scoop. Now I don't know if I've been dancing to the killer's tune this whole time.
